evidence.quote: Earlier today the Federal Open Market Committee announced a ½ percentage point reduction in the target range for the federal funds rate, bringing that range to 1 to 1¼ percent.
Against this background, the Committee judged that the risks to the U.S. outlook have changed materially.
we will continue to closely monitor developments and their implications for the economic outlook, and we will use our tools and act as appropriate to support the economy.
The fundamentals of the U.S. economy remain strong.
The virus and the measures that are being taken to contain it will surely weigh on economic activity both here and abroad for some time.
In terms of—in terms of moving forward, I would say that we do like our current policy stance.

parsed.rationale: The Chair announces a 50 basis point cut in response to coronavirus downside risks and signals readiness to act further. He also says the Committee likes the current stance, which tempers the forward guidance slightly, while describing economic fundamentals as still strong.
